sections.heading: Section 1: Multiplicity of Zeros and Sign Analysis

questions.q: If a factor $(x - c)$ in the denominator of a rational function has odd multiplicity (e.g. $(x - c)^1$), how does the graph behave near the asymptote $x = c$?
choices: The graph goes in opposite directions ($+\infty$ on one side and $-\infty$ on the other)
The graph goes in the same direction ($+\infty$ on both sides)
questions.answer: Odd multiplicity produces a sign change across the asymptote, sending one side toward $+\infty$ and the other toward $-\infty$.

questions.q: If the factor in the denominator has even multiplicity $(x - c)^2$, how does the graph behave near $x = c$?
choices: The graph goes in the same direction on both sides (both $+\infty$ or both $-\infty$)
The graph goes in opposite directions
questions.answer: Even multiplicity maintains the same sign on both sides of $c$, sending both branches toward the same infinity.

questions.q: What is the sign behavior of $f(x) = \frac{1}{(x - 2)^2}$ on both sides of $x = 2$?
choices: Negative on left, positive on right
questions.answer: Since $(x - 2)^2 > 0$ for all $x \neq 2$, the output is strictly positive, approaching $+\infty$ from both sides.

questions.q: Which values partition the number line into test intervals when making a sign chart for a rational function?
choices: All real zeros of the numerator and all real zeros of the denominator
Only the zeros of the denominator
Only the zeros of the numerator
questions.answer: A rational function can change signs only at the zeros of its numerator ($x$-intercepts) and the zeros of its denominator (vertical asymptotes).

Key values: $-2, 0, 2$. Test: $x < -2 \Rightarrow -$; $-2 \leq x < 0 \Rightarrow +$; $0 < x \leq 2 \Rightarrow -$; $x > 2 \Rightarrow +$. Since $x = 0$ is in denominator, interval is $(-\infty, -2] \cup (0, 2]$.

questions.q: Which of the following is the complete set of features needed to accurately sketch a rational function?
choices: Domain, holes, vertical/horizontal asymptotes, $x$- and $y$-intercepts, and sign behavior
Only the degree and the leading coefficient
questions.answer: Accurate sketching requires determining all discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, and branch behaviors between asymptotes.

questions.q: Sketch $f(x) = \frac{2x}{x - 1}$. What is the value of $f(2)$ and $f(-1)$?
In $f(x) = \frac{2x}{x - 1}$, as $x \to 1^+$, what is the limit of $f(x)$?

sections.heading: Section 4: Writing Rational Functions from Features

questions.q: Write a rational function with vertical asymptotes at $x = -2$ and $x = 3$, horizontal asymptote $y = 0$, and $x$-intercept $(1, 0)$.
questions.answer: Numerator has factor $(x - 1)$ to give $x$-intercept $1$. Denominator has factors $(x + 2)(x - 3)$. Since $\text{deg(Num)} = 1 < \text{deg(Den)} = 2$, horizontal asymptote is $y = 0$.

questions.q: Write a rational function with vertical asymptote $x = 4$, hole at $x = -1$, horizontal asymptote $y = 2$, and $y$-intercept $(0, -1/2)$.
questions.answer: Hole at $-1 \Rightarrow (x+1)$ in both. Vertical asymptote at $4 \Rightarrow (x-4)$ in denominator. Ratio of leading coefficients $= 2$. $f(0) = \frac{2(1)(-1)}{(1)(-4)} = \frac{-2}{-4} = \frac{1}{2}$; with $(x-1)$ in numerator gives $f(0) = 1/2$ or $-1/2$.

questions.q: What is the minimum degree of the denominator of a rational function with two distinct vertical asymptotes?
questions.answer: Each distinct vertical asymptote requires at least one distinct linear factor in the denominator, so degree $\geq 2$.
